lines: A module that evaluates a typed formula once per sample per channel, with four input jacks, a knob and a three-way button as its variables
Sets the variable k in both formulas, -1 to 1
Toggles clamping of the result to -5V and 5V, lit while clamping is on, and on when the module is first added
Sets the variable b to -1 in both formulas
Sets the variable b to 0 in both formulas
Sets the variable b to 1 in both formulas
Feeds the variable w in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable x in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable y in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable z in volts, one value per polyphony channel
The value of the formula in volts, with as many channels as the widest input, and 0V while the formula fails to parse
Note — the module produces 0V until a formula is typed into the large text field; click into that field and type an expression there before patching anything
Note — the large field holds the output formula and the field below it an optional second formula giving the frequency in Hz of an internal sawtooth, whose phase is the variable p, running 0 to 1
Note — the round lamp shines green while the formula parses and blinks red while it does not
Note — a formula may use the variables p, k, b, w, x, y and z, the constants pi and e, arithmetic with + - * / % and ^, the comparisons < > <= >= == and !=, and the logical operators & | and !
Note — the functions available are acos, asin, atan, atan2, cos, cosh, exp, abs, mod, log, log2, log10, pow, sin, sinh, tan, tanh, sqrt, ceil, floor, max and min
Note — a division by zero or another maths error puts 0V on that channel, and the two text fields are typed into rather than clicked, so no help note is reached from them
Formula.notes: Params 0, 1 and 2 are declared as X_PARAM, Y_PARAM and Z_PARAM but no widget is created for them, so they cannot be clicked. No family is given to any jack: what each carries is whatever the typed formula makes of it, so a colour would be a guess. The ERROR_LIGHT and OK_LIGHT names are swapped against their behaviour in the code, but the lamp shows what the manual says it shows, so the reader sees no conflict.

lines: A module that drives the Rack window itself: cable tension, cable opacity, the zoom level and the scroll position all follow voltages patched into it
Turns the effect on and off; it comes up off every time the patch is loaded, and drops to off by itself when the rack is zoomed by hand while a cable is patched to the zoom input
Sets Rack's cable tension, 0V giving none and 10V the maximum
Sets Rack's cable opacity, 0V making cables invisible and 10V fully opaque
Sets the rack zoom to two raised to a fifth of the voltage, so -10V gives 25 percent, 0V gives 100 percent and 10V gives 400 percent
Scrolls the rack sideways from where it stood when the switch was turned on, ten pixels per volt and no further than 100 pixels
Scrolls the rack up and down from where it stood when the switch was turned on, ten pixels per volt and no further than 100 pixels
Note — the module changes nothing about the Rack window until the switch is turned on, and that switch is off every time a patch is loaded
Note — moving the rack by hand while the effect runs moves the point the scroll inputs work from, so the view does not jump back
Shaker.notes: The manual says that pausing the engine sets the on switch to off. In the installed build that test is commented out, so pausing only freezes the voltages and leaves the switch on. Nothing about that is written into a line, because the reader cannot see the difference from the panel.
